title: The Mysterious Sky Trumpets That Terrified Whole Towns

basis.note: median of recent videos blended with the niche benchmark; learning gated until day 5

predicted_range.basis: about 3x either way, from backtested error (93 of our own videos so far)

segments.narration: People woke up to deafening brass horns in the clouds. No instruments caused the noise.
Audio recordings captured loud trumpet-like blasts vibrating windowpanes across entire neighborhoods.
The strange sounds left observers without a clear explanation, often leading them to perceive the phenomenon as mysterious.
Researchers have proposed several potential explanations for the phenomenon, though no single origin has been positively identified.
Proposed explanations range from gas explosions and meteors to atmospheric ducting of distant sounds.

accuracy_flags.claim: The sounds baffled scientists and sparked viral internet panic.
accuracy_flags.note: The article states those who experience skyquakes typically do not have a clear explanation and perceive them as mysterious, but viral internet panic is an overstatement and sensationalized embellishment not present in the text.

accuracy_flags.claim: Researchers linked the phenomenon to atmospheric pressure waves called skyquakes.
accuracy_flags.note: The article explicitly states that their origin has not been positively identified and no proposal has been experimentally confirmed, though several hypotheses exist. Saying researchers 'linked' it implies a settled scientific consensus.

accuracy_flags.claim: Severe weather creates infrasound waves that human ears convert into metallic groans.
accuracy_flags.note: The text lists various hypotheses (like weather, meteors, gas explosions, etc.), but it does not state that severe weather forces infrasound waves downward that human ears convert into metallic groans.
